## Test-count parity evidence (AC 5, operator-attested)

The two pytest summary lines, both `pytest -m "not integration and not external" -q -p no:randomly` in this worktree:

PRE-SPLIT (clean tree at origin/main 3834269c53):
    1 failed, 10284 passed, 46 skipped, 222 deselected, 36 warnings in 3330.68s (0:55:30)

POST-SPLIT (at the split commit, stable HEAD):
    1 failed, 10292 passed, 38 skipped, 222 deselected, 36 warnings in 2298.56s (0:38:18)

Totals are equal: 1 + 10284 + 46 = 10331 = 1 + 10292 + 38. The 8 tests that moved from skipped to passed are HEAD-conditional (they skip when history carries no ticket-referencing commit; the baseline ran on a tree with no local commit, the post-split run at the split commit). No test changed outcome because of the refactor, and the single failure is identical in both runs: tests/unit/grounding/test_coverage_reconstruction.py::test_full_backend_account_is_present, an opengrep-backend failure already confirmed pre-existing on clean origin/main by other agents on this host.

Because that skip/pass split is environment-dependent, here is a stronger parity proof that is not: `pytest --collect-only` on a throwaway detached worktree at the baseline commit vs the post-split tree gives **10328/10550 collected, 222 deselected on BOTH**, and a sorted diff of the two collected test-ID lists is **empty** — zero tests added, removed or renamed.

An earlier post-split run additionally reported 1 error (schema-coverage teardown, 'Test moved the repo HEAD 3834269c53 -> 29b5a4ed1d'). That was self-inflicted: I committed while that run was in flight. The clean re-run above has no error.
